Relocatable paths

paths implements the directory rules from config at 32650ae5. The process's real uid selects the default tier: uid 0 is system; every other uid is user. Where the binary is installed does not select the tier.

RootOverrideWhole-tree $MIXOSUser defaultSystem default
prefixMIXOS_PREFIXIgnoredParent of the running binary's bin/Same
shareMIXOS_SHARE (absolute only)Ignored<prefix>/shareSame
etcMIXOS_ETC$MIXOS/etc$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mixos, else ~/.config/mixos/etc/mixos
varMIXOS_VAR$MIXOS/var$XDG_DATA_HOME/mixos, else ~/.local/share/mixos/var/lib/mixos
runMIXOS_RUN$MIXOS/run$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/mixos, else /tmp/mixos-run/run/mixos
cacheMIXOS_CACHE$MIXOS/cache$XDG_CACHE_HOME/mixos, else ~/.cache/mixos/var/cache/mixos

An empty variable is unset. Relative XDG variables are ignored. The original etc, var and run overrides and $MIXOS retain main's acceptance of relative values; callers that previously required absolute application directories still enforce that requirement. An absent HOME falls back to /root, as in main.

Per-root precedence is its override variable, then $MIXOS where applicable, then <prefix>/layout.mx, then the uid default. Prefix itself comes only from MIXOS_PREFIX or /proc/self/exe, following symlinks to the real executable. layout.mx is bounded strict data with at most five keys: etc, var, run, share, cache. A prefix key is refused. Root values in that file must be absolute paths without .. or control bytes. Unknown and duplicate keys refuse. A root in layout.mx applies to every uid, like $MIXOS; it is not a system-tier override. Gold writes only roots differing from the selected tier's defaults for the target prefix (system unless --tier user) and removes layout.mx when there are no differences. A default system install therefore retains user XDG directories even with the system prefix.

etc: "/srv/example/etc"
var: "/srv/example/var"

Process helpers cache one environment and layout snapshot for the process. Environment plus Dirs::from_source provide pure env/uid/executable inputs; Dirs::from_environment additionally reads the layout file. config::Dir, config::Environment, config::Dirs and config::path are thin re-exports. There is one implementation. Compatibility fixtures spell out the expected values for both uids at two installation prefixes.

Rust uses paths::root(paths::Root::Etc), paths::bin("mix"), paths::share("scenes/editor") and paths::resolve("mixos:share/scenes"). Fallible callers use try_root, try_system and resolve; the infallible helpers document their startup expect contract. paths::system(Root::Etc) selects system defaults regardless of uid, retaining override precedence. system_default explicitly ignores process overrides for existing APIs whose contract was a fixed system fallback, such as the native bus endpoint. It also keeps webd's WWW default, blobd's fallback and indexd's database/model defaults at their existing system paths. In particular indexd's model cache stays under var/indexd/.cache; it does not move to the additive cache root.

mixos_path("etc")
mixos_path("etc", "node.conf.mix", {tier: "system"})
mixos_path("var", "example", {tier: "user"})
mixos_path("mixos:share/scenes/editor/scene.mix")

Logical references use mixos:<root>/<relative> with the six names above. Relative tails cannot escape their root. Ordinary user file paths are unchanged. Existing per-file overrides such as MIXOS_NODE_CONFIG stay in place.

Application state keeps its existing policy. AppDirs, Ced, Dopus and screenshot retain MIXOS_APP_HOME, MIXOS_APPS_HOME, MIXOS_VAR/apps, XDG state and home state precedence; config/state/cache remain children of that application root. The macro catalogue keeps its own XDG config directory and MIXOS_MIX override. These policies do not switch to the directory resolver's XDG data default.

External files use @{prefix}, @{share}, @{etc}, @{var}, @{run} and @{cache} templates. Template sources ship under share/layout/; output stays in its packaged place inside the prefix, including share/<component>/units/ and share/applications/. The unmanaged flat share/units/ tree is never changed. mix layout apply [--root SYSROOT] [--dry-run] [--image] renders them idempotently, prints changed files and manages a single link to <prefix>/bin/mix: /usr/local/bin/mix on hosts, /usr/bin/mix only in a MixOS-owned image. On a host it adds the link to /etc/shells. It does not manage mixrc or enable services. --image requires --root; with --root, no host or HOME files are touched, and only --image adds staged /etc/shells. An image root must resolve to a directory other than /; aliases to / refuse. An unprivileged apply without --root still renders its own prefix. When it cannot write both host targets it skips the link and shells line with a notice. A non-symlink at the link refuses. The staging root is canonicalised before checking its children. Symlink parents below it and symlink render targets refuse. Every target is checked before the first write. Existing file modes and owners survive; new files are 0644. Exec and Environment paths are quoted when needed; whitespace in a path used by a systemd key that does not unquote (such as EnvironmentFile, ConditionPathExists or LoadCredential) refuses. Desktop TryExec takes the rest of its line as a literal path, so a spaced prefix renders there unquoted. mix-static is never linked. Host Elixir installs do not rename this entry.

Installers select a target independently of their interpreter. The staged binary prints defaults from this same Rust implementation without self-location, layout files or MIXOS overrides:

/path/to/staged/mix layout defaults --tier system --json
/path/to/staged/mix layout defaults --tier user --prefix /home/user/mixos --json

System installation defaults use /opt/mixos; user installation requires --prefix. Both commands return six roots, including the user run fallback. tools/gold_release.mix and tools/component_install.mix accept --prefix and optional --share, --etc, --var, --run, --cache, --tier roots. Explicit target flags precede its layout file, then the staged binary's defaults. They do not inherit the installer's ambient layout overrides. Component --root is a staging sysroot; --mix STAGED_MIX supplies defaults before a target binary exists. Gold verifies the release before querying its binary, renders the owned staged files before hashing, journals any non-default layout document and saves all six target roots in receipts. Per-package template manifests coexist, so desktop and server install together. The packaged notifyd and releasesd unit copies render in share/<component>/units/; component_install continues to own and record the separate lib and systemd copies. They remain excluded from the global source manifest. Release records are beneath var/releases. Rollback/recovery can use --receipt-file FILE without invoking a target binary. At the default layout there is no layout.mx. Give --var to locate receipts (or use --receipt-file); a non-default layout file can also supply var:

mix tools/gold_release.mix rollback --prefix /opt/mixos --var /var/lib/mixos --receipt ID
mix tools/gold_release.mix recover --prefix /opt/mixos --var /var/lib/mixos

Emergency installs of older archives whose binary lacks layout defaults require all six roots explicitly. Gold reports the older archive and persists all five non-prefix roots rather than guessing defaults. Without all six flags it refuses. For a current binary, the baseline uses the selected --tier. Gold also journals the host entrance: prior link target or absence and prior shells hash, with original bytes and metadata in the release backup. Failed installs, rollback and recovery restore those states, refusing subsequent drift. Receipt entrance targets are restricted to the link and shells, with a fixed sysroot marker for isolated tests; receipts cannot introduce arbitrary paths. Main's earlier absolute root/backup receipts without a layout are also readable, including release ordering; their shapes are retained during rollback.

Repository tools work under the previous release and mix-static. Docs resolve logical paths against the checkout: mixos:share/x names <repo>/share/x. Populate pinned font inputs with mix share/assets/install.mix --root /absolute/checkout/share/assets; these ignored build inputs are excluded from packages. Lint skips installed-asset checks when mixos_path is unavailable.

To relocate, stop affected processes, move the prefix, update non-default roots in layout.mx, render again and restart. Existing processes retain their cached snapshot. This implementation does not migrate live data. tools/layout_migrate_saved.mix --source COPY --from-prefix OLD_PREFIX --from-layout OLD_LAYOUT previews offline changes by default; --apply keeps originals. Token boundaries prevent replacing roots embedded inside other paths. Colon is not a left boundary, so /usr/bin:/opt/mixos/bin:/bin stays unchanged; assignment boundaries using = are still accepted. An interrupted apply can resume when the retained original still equals the unmigrated file; a different original refuses. Dry-run never removes temporaries. The old layout supplies the five non-prefix roots. SQLite stores must first be exported by their owner so revisions and audit chains survive.

The gate rejects literal roots outside resolver defaults, templates, default assertions and documentation. The release proof uses a prefix with a space and a private mount namespace hiding the old roots. Installer, scene, nested desk and SSH loopback tests use disposable roots; unavailable privileges report a clear skip. Units, desktop entries and runtime relocation all run under the spaced prefix. The template proof compares 37 global and 8 component-owned templates byte-for-byte with main; --installed additionally reports drift in existing packaged targets. It does not inspect or change unmanaged flat unit copies. Templates not included in a selected release, such as dnsd's EnvironmentFile with a prefix path, can require a prefix without whitespace. Unit/runtime relocation still uses a prefix with a space; desktop rendering requires a prefix without whitespace.

Three fixed-FHS Mix defaults remain as exact path-gate deferrals: bridged's system config fallback, scene-sync's session environment file, and topbar's identity file. Their original per-file/CLI overrides remain authoritative. Using a tier lookup there would newly honour MIXOS or layout overrides and would not preserve main's selection. tools/path_gate_exceptions.mx records each line and its reason. An isolated relocation run must supply their original overrides if it exercises these paths; these defaults are not relocation proof. The same registry retains the two literal storage paths in indexd's shipped example: its loader does not resolve logical strings, and changing their tier would change the database/model locations. The registry has five exact lines in four files; it may shrink, and cannot grow silently.
